title: 1D Motion: Displacement, Velocity & Constant Acceleration Equations

authority_basis.claim_scope: Pinned PR383 Class 9 Chapter 8 source record for rectilinear motion under constant acceleration.

concepts.statement: For constant acceleration a: v = u + at, s = ut + (1/2)at^2, v^2 = u^2 + 2as.
concepts.why_required: Governs rectilinear motion under constant acceleration.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Equations applied to variable acceleration without calculus.

conditions: Signs follow the chosen 1D axis coordinate system.

model_conditions.physical_reason: Kinematic algebraic equations are derived assuming da/dt = 0.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Using the algebraic relation with variable acceleration produces incorrect velocity and position trajectories.

representations.semantic_geometry: A 1D coordinate axis encodes an origin, positive direction, and signed velocity and acceleration directions.
must_not_imply: the sign convention may be omitted
representations.verification_method: Verify velocity and acceleration directions against the declared positive 1D axis.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Choose origin and positive coordinate direction.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Velocity and acceleration signs become ambiguous.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify known variables (u, v, a, s, t).
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Equation selection can introduce multiple unresolved unknowns.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Select kinematic equation containing one unknown.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: A relation may be applied without matching the known and unknown variables.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Applying v = u + at to motion with time-varying acceleration.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Treating kinematic equations as universally valid for all motions.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Show the declared 1D axis together with the constant-acceleration condition before applying the algebraic kinematic relation.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce constant acceleration precondition before using standard kinematic equations.
misconceptions.verification: Reject the algebraic constant-acceleration relation when acceleration varies with time.

problem_families.name: Rectilinear Uniform Acceleration Trajectory
recognition_cues: Find stopping distance or travel time under constant acceleration
problem_families.first_technical_move: Set up coordinate axis and apply kinematic equation

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Applying kinematic equations when acceleration is variable.
